text:
Anya: Quick share — I ran the quant holdback experiments for the new 13B model (int8 baseline vs int6 candidate) using a signal-split (50/50) on the GTN traffic slice. Short summary: int6 reduces token cost ~20% but shows a 3.2% drop on our answer-quality score (Pass@1 variant) concentrated on multi-turn clarifications and long-context retrieval. Want take on whether to canary or hold. Full micro-summary below.

Matt: can you paste the numbers?

Anya: sure, here's the micro-summary
```
model,quant,latency_p95(ms),cost_per_1k_tokens,qa_delta(pass@1)
13B-v1,int8,210, $0.95, 0.0%
13B-v1,int6,220, $0.76, -3.2%
hybrid(short->int6,long->int8),varies,230, $0.84, -0.4% (+routing overhead)
```
Notes: latency p95 includes routing overhead; cost is proxy using current price sheet; qa_delta is relative to int8 baseline on the sampled GTN slice.

Li: 3.2% drop is > our regression threshold (1.5%). Do we know which prompts cause the regressions?

Anya: yes — concentrated on:
- multi-turn clarifications (avg history >3 turns)
- retrieval-heavy queries with >512 tokens of context
Examples: "Resolve ambiguous user intent across convo" and long multi-doc summarization where the model hallucinates an extra entity.

Sasha: if drop is concentrated, hybrid routing seems promising. What's the engineering complexity/overhead for short-vs-long routing? and did you simulate a threshold?

Anya: simulated simple length-based routing: if input_tokens <= 512 -> int6 else int8. That yields ~12% cost savings on overall traffic (because 60% of queries are short) and qa delta -0.4% on our slice. Engineering overhead: routing flag + extra call path, ~1.2% tail latency penalty in steady state (measured in synthetic test). We also measured KV cache hit reduction on long-turns when routing toggles models; impact seems small but needs canary.

Product Sam: from product/GTN POV, a -0.4% QA hit is probably acceptable if we pass on cost (savings >10% net). But we need to validate on top-product queries (billing, search, onboarding flows) — those are sensitive.

Matt: ops ask: how would rollback work? Recommend canary 5% traffic with active QA monitoring (pass@1 over rolling 24h). Abort if QA delta >1% and SLO tail latency >+5%.

Li: agree to extra targeted evals — I'll run the top-product query subset and multi-turn sims overnight and deliver a short scorecard.

Sasha: I'll open a feature flag and canary plan. ops-bot, create flag and schedule.

ops-bot: Created feature flag `quant_short_routing_int6` — owner: Sasha — canary window: 4h -> 24h. /flag

Anya: action items: 1) Li run targeted evals and post scorecard, 2) Sasha & Matt set up canary + rollback hooks, 3) Product Sam approves canary if Li's scorecard shows QA delta <= 1% on product queries. I'll hold off wide rollout until we validate.

Product Sam: sounds good. please include a couple of high-fidelity examples in Li's scorecard so we can sample qualitatively.

Matt: if all green after 24h at 5% canary, we scale to 20% with A/B for 48h, then decide full rollout.

Anya: thanks — I'll ping here once Li's scorecard and the canary infra are ready. :thumbsup:

Li: will post results by 09:30 PT tomorrow.

Sasha: flag and bake plan in place. I'll DM infra for tracing tweaks.

ops-bot: Reminder: canary alert template created on channel eng-ml-incidents for QA delta > 1%.

Anya: one more note — we also ran int4 on a small sample: huge QoL regressions on long-form, so not recommended. Keeping that out of scope for now.

Matt: good call. keep int4 in the lab.

Sasha: thanks all — moving to canary prep.
